items.front: What kind of tree results from inserting keys into a BST in sorted order, and why?
items.back: A degenerate tree: it is effectively a linked list, because each key goes to one side of the previous node.

items.front: What is the search cost in a degenerate BST built by inserting keys in sorted order?
items.back: O(n), since the tree has height n.

items.front: What is the height of a degenerate BST with n keys inserted in sorted order?
items.back: About n, since it becomes effectively a linked list.

items.front: What order does an in-order traversal visit the parts of a BST?
items.back: Left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree.

items.front: What property do the keys have when output by an in-order traversal of a BST?
items.back: They are yielded in sorted order.
